headline: Biomedical knowledge graphs are being grounded in evidence and corrected for hub bias
label: Evidence Grounded Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
summary: Recent preprints pair knowledge-graph reasoning with PubMed evidence, uncertainty propagation and topology correction for hypothesis generation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is making knowledge-graph reasoning more evidence-aware and less distorted by graph structure. SPIDER grounds graph relations in PubMed evidence and maintains SPIDER-KG as an incrementally updated resource, while BiomedCAT derives user-shaped RTX-KG2c subgraphs from biomedical slides to support mechanistic hypothesis generation. The uncertainty-conditioned path-energy framework maps genomic model predictions over AlzKB and Hetionet to phenotype hypotheses. Topological correction appears in two items: Inverse Node Frequency normalises metapath features to reduce hub bias in target-adverse event prediction, and BRIDGE propagates genetic evidence over coupled protein and disease networks, raising target-indication coverage from 5.1% to 9.5%. SigMatch systematically evaluates how sample tissue biases transcriptomic disease-relationship predictions across correlation and rank measures. The tasks and methods differ, so the shared element is provenance, scoping and topological correction rather than a common architecture.
